_because: 2026-09-04: the corpus grew, so the counts fell. This checker asks 'does anything reach this?', and on 2026-09-04 the operator's apps moved into apps/, its own git repository, invisible to the platform's git ls-files. Five platform surfaces then read as dead having lost no caller at all: the app shell helpers and both chat docks (imported by app module.tsx through the @shell/ seam), services.app_persona (imported by three app personas), and the relay API area. The fix was to the SCAN, not to the pins -- nested-repo tracked files are in the corpus now, app Python imports count as imports, and reachability through @shell/ is followed transitively. Pinning those five as deliberately-dead would have been false and would have hidden them the next time they really did die. Net: frontend 4->1, backend 19->17, api areas 3->2.

services.triager.why: PINNED BECAUSE THE CHECKER CANNOT SEE ITS CALLER, NOT BECAUSE IT IS DEAD. services.triager is the role runner for `role: triager` agents and is reached from SHELL: scripts/dispatch_triggers.sh:549 does `from services import triager` inside a heredoc and :550 calls triager.has_due_notes(), with :588 registering it in ROLE_HANDLERS; scripts/triager_run.sh:96 execs `python3 -m services.triager`. This scan counts Python imports only, so a shell-mediated import is invisible to it.
services.triager.do_not: Do not read this pin as agreement that the module is dead. On 2026-09-04 BACKLOG-MEASURED-2026-09-04.md row 13 ordered it deleted on exactly that misreading, using a grep scoped to backend/. Ticket 88a2ba81 exists to give it a live trigger.
services.triager.unpin_when: the scan learns to follow imports out of scripts/*.sh
